parts.article:
Surviving city life
 
Although the colonisation of Australia profoundly affected the continent's natural environment, many plants and animals have actually flourished since European settlement. Some even thrive in the concrete jungle of Australia's biggest city, Sydney.
 
A Ecologists often prefer to study plants and animals in exotic locations, but a growing number have turned their attention to the complex interactions of the wildlife that inhabits concrete jungles. Inner-city Sydney is the laboratory of choice for a number of ecologists, and their research is timely. More than half the world's human population resides in cities, and urban development continues to increase all over the world. By 2030, the United Nations projects five billion people will live in cities. Associate Professor Dieter Hochuli, a biologist at the University of Sydney, believes that 'we need to understand how cities are changing the ecology of the systems they are built on, and how plants and animals are adapting to them'.
 
B If any species has learnt to thrive in an urban environment, it's the native white ibis. A strange long-legged bird with a bow-shaped beak, it is known as the 'garbage turkey'. The bird's reputation for digging through inner-city bins and scavenging street garbage has not endeared it to the public. The white ibis began its move to the city in the 1970s, when large parts of its natural habitat of inland wetlands became degraded due to years of low rainfall. 'The species is a wetland forager,' wildlife officer John Martin from Sydney's Royal Botanic Gardens says. 'Now it happily forages in city parks and landfill.' During the peak of its spring breeding season, there are more than 9 000 of these birds in Sydney.
 
C Specimens at Sydney's Australian Museum show that the city's overall bird life has changed dramatically over the two centuries since colonisation. Prior to urban development, Sydney's native bushland was populated by large numbers of small insect-eating birds, such as the superb fairy-wren and the eastern yellow robin. Today, homeowners prefer to landscape their backyards with tall trees and manicured lawns—an environment that provides little protection for small birds. But one bird's trash is another's treasure. Gardens filled with flowering plants and fruit trees favour omnivorous birds such as currawongs, bowerbirds and the city's most despised resident – the noisy miner. 'They're a real winner in cities,' Australian Museum ornithologist Richard Major says. 'The predominant driver in the decline of small birds is that we've made a suitable environment for native noisy miners.'
 
D Many invertebrates, such as the golden orb-weaver spider and the blue triangle butterfly, also relish living in the city. The golden orb spiders in Sydney are fatter and fitter than species found elsewhere, and Professor Hochuli and his team are trying to understand why. 'We're trying to determine whether it's more food or the urban heat – as it's up to four degrees warmer in the city.' Hochuli has also found some varieties of ant more at home in the city. 'The green ant, known for its painful bite, will build a nest where there is space and food, regardless of whether it's a backyard or a sports oval.' 'It's remarkable how many things persist in city environments,' he says. The decline in birds that eat small invertebrates means these populations grow unchecked, allowing them to chew their way through the foliage of the city's trees.
 
E While some species can survive in relatively small areas, mammals have been confined to patches of bushland scattered around Sydney and its nearby national parks. However, the rabbit-sized, long-nosed bandicoot has discovered the advantages of venturing out to grassy suburban backyards and gardens. 'They forage for invertebrates in the grass and like the surrounding habitat to nest and escape from predators,' Catherine Price, a research associate at the University of Sydney, says. Dr Price is trying to understand what encourages the little mammal into urban environments. 'We don't know if it's an overflow from the park, or if they've got particular survival traits that allow them to evade dogs and cats, and use the urban habitat that benefits them,' she says.
 
F It's not just native wildlife that has sought comfort in city living. Non-native species such as black rodents, cockroaches and foxes have developed survival strategies too. But weeds are the pest that has gained the most advantage. 'In residential Sydney there would not be a single area of remnant bushland not infested by introduced plant life,' Michelle Leishman, a Macquarie University plant biologist, says. Over 20 years, Leishman and her colleagues have shown how Sydney's huge stretches of impermeable concrete, together with the storm-water system, have helped weeds infiltrate the few remaining pockets of bushland. As rain washes over backyards and roadways, it collects chemicals which enter the storm-water system, where they are piped to the edges of bushland. The nutrient-rich water seeps into the earth, favouring the many exotic species that 'live fast and die young,' Leishman says. Indigenous plants prefer low-fertility soil and struggle to cope with one that is more fertile.

analyses.content: 这一段重点在于“ecologists turn their attention to...”（生态学家将注意力转向……），强调的是研究的动机，而不是具体的环境变化。
(Paragraph A) "Associate Professor Dieter Hochuli... believes that 'we need to understand how cities are changing the ecology of the systems they are built on...'"
A段最后引用 Dieter Hochuli 的话说“我们需要了解城市如何改变生态系统”，这正是科学家对研究城市区域感兴趣的原因，对应选项 vi。
B段全篇都在描述“white ibis（白鹮）”这种鸟，它被称为“garbage turkey（垃圾火鸡）”，喜欢在垃圾箱里翻找食物，对应选项 iv（一种喜欢垃圾的生物）。
看到“garbage turkey”和“digging through bins”就能直接对应“likes rubbish”。
(Paragraph B) "...it is known as the 'garbage turkey'. The bird's reputation for digging through inner-city bins and scavenging street garbage..."
C段对比了城市化前后鸟类的变化，指出花园环境（built environments）导致小型鸟类减少，却鼓励了 noisy miners 等特定物种（particular species）的繁衍，对应选项 vii。
不要选 ii（imported flora and fauna），因为本段讨论的 noisy miners 和 small birds 都是 native（本土的），重点在于建筑环境对不同物种的筛选作用。
(Paragraph C) "The predominant driver in the decline of small birds is that we've made a suitable environment for native noisy miners."
虽然蜘蛛（spider）严格来说不是昆虫（insect），但在雅思标题中通常归为一类理解，且段落中也提到了蚂蚁（ant）和蝴蝶（butterfly）。
D段列举了蜘蛛、蝴蝶、蚂蚁等无脊椎动物在城市中“relish living（享受生活）”，长得更肥更壮，对应选项 iii（在城市区域繁荣的昆虫）。
(Paragraph D) "Many invertebrates, such as the golden orb-weaver spider and the blue triangle butterfly, also relish living in the city."
E段描述了长鼻袋狸（long-nosed bandicoot）这种小动物离开灌木丛，“venturing out（冒险进入）”后院草坪，扩大了活动范围，对应选项 i（小动物扩张领地）。
重点在于“expanding its territory”，对应原文的“venturing out to grassy suburban backyards”。
(Paragraph E) "However, the rabbit-sized, long-nosed bandicoot has discovered the advantages of venturing out to grassy suburban backyards and gardens."
F段解释了城市的硬质地面（concrete）和排水系统如何帮助杂草（weeds）和引进物种（introduced plant life）渗透蔓延，对应选项 ii（城市环境鼓励引进动植物的传播）。
这里的关键词是“imported flora”（引进植物/杂草）和“spread”（蔓延/infiltrate），与 C 段的本土物种区分开。
(Paragraph F) "...Sydney's huge stretches of impermeable concrete... have helped weeds infiltrate the few remaining pockets of bushland."

analyses.content: (Paragraph E) "'We don't know if it's an overflow from the park, or if they've got particular survival traits...' she says."
“We don't know” 直接对应题目中的 “It is not clear”。
E段中 Catherine Price (D) 在谈到袋狸时说“We don't know if it's an overflow... or if they've got particular survival traits...”，表示原因尚不清楚，选 D。

questions.question: Hot weather might positively affect the health of a species.

analyses.content: D段中 Dieter Hochuli (A) 指出城市的蜘蛛比其他地方的“fatter and fitter（更肥更健康）”，并推测原因可能是“urban heat（城市热岛效应）”，选 A。
“Fatter and fitter” 对应 “positively affect health”，“urban heat” 对应 “hot weather”。
(Paragraph D) "'We're trying to determine whether it's more food or the urban heat – as it's up to four degrees warmer in the city.'"

questions.question: Sydney's residential gardens suit some species better than others.

analyses.content: C段中 Richard Major (C) 指出我们建造的环境（backyards with tall trees...）导致小型鸟类减少，却成为了 noisy miners 的“suitable environment”，选 C。
“Suit some species better than others” 对应原文中 noisy miners 是赢家（winner），而 small birds 是输家（decline）。
(Paragraph C) "'The predominant driver in the decline of small birds is that we've made a suitable environment for native noisy miners.' ... Richard Major says."

questions.question: Research into the natural world's responses to urban settings is vital.

analyses.content: (Paragraph A) "Associate Professor Dieter Hochuli... believes that 'we need to understand how cities are changing the ecology of the systems they are built on...'"
A段末尾 Dieter Hochuli (A) 强调“we need to understand how cities are changing the ecology...”，表达了研究的必要性和重要性，选 A。
题目中的 “vital” 对应原文强烈的语气 “we need to understand”。注意题目提示“NB You may use any letter more than once”，这里 A 用了两次。

groups.contentHtml: It's not only native plants and animals that are adapting to city life; non-native plants and animals are also adapting. Examples of successful 'city dwellers' include small, non-native rats and non-native insects such as . However, what causes most problems in the city is weeds. Michelle Leishman, a scientist from Macquarie University, has proven that Sydney's large areas of and its drainage network favour the growth of weeds. Water gathers as it passes from gardens and streets into the city drainage network. This, in turn, creates very good soil for several varieties of rapidly growing non-native plants.

analyses.content: 题目要求举例非本土昆虫（non-native insects），原文 F 段列举了 black rodents（啮齿类，非昆虫）、foxes（狐狸，非昆虫）和 cockroaches（蟑螂，昆虫），填 cockroaches。
必须填昆虫类，black rodents 和 foxes 虽然在同一句，但属于哺乳动物。
(Paragraph F) "Non-native species such as black rodents, cockroaches and foxes have developed survival strategies too."
题目说 Sydney 大面积的____和排水网络有利于杂草生长，原文提到“Sydney's huge stretches of impermeable concrete”，填 concrete。
题目中的“large areas”对应原文的“huge stretches”，注意单词拼写。
(Paragraph F) "...Sydney's huge stretches of impermeable concrete, together with the storm-water system..."
题目说水在流经花园和街道时收集了____，原文说“it collects chemicals which enter the storm-water system”，填 chemicals。
动词“gathers”对应原文的“collects”，直接定位宾语。
(Paragraph F) "As rain washes over backyards and roadways, it collects chemicals which enter the storm-water system..."
